Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).

six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every closed immersion of schemes is finite, hence
proper; the empty closed immersion is included, no Noetherian, reducedness or
nonemptiness hypothesis is used, and the Axiom of Choice enters through the
affine quotient structure of closed immersions and the properness of finite
morphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Purity of the diagonal and its positive Thom class. By [F2] one has $\omega_{M\times M}=k_{M\times M}[4d]$ and $\omega_M=k_M[2d]$, and dualizing transitivity in [F1] gives $\Delta^!\omega_{M\times M}=\omega_M$; hence $\Delta^!k_{M\times M}=\Delta^!\omega_{M\times M}[-4d]=\omega_M[-4d]=k_M[-2d]$. The exceptional restriction along the diagonal is therefore concentrated in the single cohomological degree $2d$, and the normalization of [F2] singles out its generator: in a complex normal chart the pair is $(\mathbb C^d,\mathbb C^d\setminus\{0\})$ and the positive compactly supported generator of the ball evaluates to $+1$ on the positively oriented relative class of degree $2d$, so the local generators are uniquely determined and no higher-degree ambiguity exists. A complex-linear chart transition has positive real determinant, so the local positive generators glue to a global class; the resulting class $\tau_\Delta:k_{M\times M}\to\Delta_*k_M[2d]$ is the positive middle-diagonal Thom class, and the isomorphism $\Delta^!k_{M\times M}\cong k_M[-2d]$ is the associated orientation.

The pulled-back Thom class on the support. By [F4] the diagonal is proper, and the square relating $F=(q,u)$, $\Delta$, $\theta$ and the projection $\gamma:T\to M$ is Cartesian by construction of $T=A\times_MB$. Proper base change of [F1] therefore identifies $F^*\Delta_*k_M[2d]\cong\theta_*\gamma^*k_M[2d]=\theta_*k_T[2d]$; pushing the Thom class of step 1.1 through this identification gives a global class $\tau_F:k_{A\times B}\to\theta_*k_T[2d]$ supported on $T$. Capping a Borel–Moore class of $A\times B$ with $\tau_F$ is defined for arbitrary closed supports: it uses only the ambient orientation of the smooth diagonal and the support of $\tau_F$, makes no transversality assertion about $T$ inside $A\times B$, and lowers Borel–Moore degree by exactly $2d$ because $\tau_F$ has cohomological degree $2d$.

Supported evaluation identifies the refined operation with the exchange mate. Let $\theta:T\hookrightarrow A\times B$ be the closed support embedding with open complement $j$, so that the localization clause of [F1] gives the exact triangle $\theta_!\theta^!\to\operatorname{id}\to j_*j^*$ (equivalently $j_!j^!\to\operatorname{id}\to\theta_*\theta^*$). Applying $R\operatorname{Hom}(k_{A\times B},-)$ and using the adjunction $\theta^*\dashv\theta_*$ identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}(\theta_*k_T,G)$ with the relative sections $R\Gamma_T(G)$: on a closed support, exceptional restriction is computed by sections supported there, and tensor evaluation realizes the cup/cap product of supported classes as the tensor–Hom evaluation map. Running the two external classes through the Cartesian square with maps $(a,b;q,u)$ exhibits the base-change morphism $u^*q_!\to b_!a^*$ and its mate $\mathrm{ex}:a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$; by construction its defining adjunction equalities are precisely the evaluation of $\tau_F$ under tensor–Hom adjunction together with dualizing transitivity. The agreement is thus an equality of the two explicit adjoint maps, not an inference from equality after forgetting supports, and it uses no transversality of the support.

Ordered iterated diagonals. For two ordered smooth middle factors the normal model of the product diagonal is the ordered direct sum of the two complex normal bundles, and on the product of normal coordinate disks the relative cup product of the two positive generators evaluates to $+1$ on the ordered product disk, which is the positive generator of the direct sum; local uniqueness as in step 1.1 and base-change mate pasting as in steps 2.1 and 3.1 therefore give the composed refined operation on every support, in the given order and without an interchange of factors. All real degrees involved are even, so reordering the two complex summands introduces no sign: the only possible sign is $(-1)^{(2d_1)(2d_2)}=+1$. The equivariant form holds verbatim by [F3], which supplies the same localization, exchange and normalized orientation clauses in $D^b_{G,c}$, with $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ rather than a quotient-stack shift.

Zero sections and Euler classes. Let $\pi:V\to X$ be a complex vector bundle of rank $c$ with zero section $s:X\hookrightarrow V$; the normal bundle of $s$ is $V$ itself, and steps 1.1 and 2.1 apply with $M=X$, $d=c$. Pulling the positive Thom class back along the zero section gives the oriented Euler class $e(V)\in H^{2c}(X;k)$, by definition the zero-section restriction of the complex-oriented Thom class; consequently applying the refined zero-section pullback after the zero-section pushforward is cap product with $e(V)$, compatibly with the orientation normalization and with proper pushforward and Cartesian pullback by the projection formula and trace/base-change mates of [F1]. This is the standard oriented Euler class attached to the given complex orientation; on CW-type approximations it agrees with the top Chern class by the published Euler-to-top-Chern identification used later on this page. All constructions are those of steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 with the declared suppliers, and AC is used only through [A1].

[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
gives a locally small triangulated category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with conservative
restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift, and its morphism groups are
computed by the coinduced simplicial injectives of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]. Locally
split free-action descent identifies its finite general linear Stiefel
resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$, and
the bounded Hom and image comparisons, the degree-zero ring comparison and
retract closure of
[[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]
hold for it. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$. The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$u^*v^!\to v'^!u'^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$u'_!v'^*\cong v^*u_!$. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is consumed exactly through the three cited suppliers, whose
constructions (equivariant descent, injective replacements, Borel stabilization) declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_p\to Z_m$. The maps $q_p:Z_p\to X$,
$q_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=g_1\cdots g_px$, satisfy $q_p\circ Z_\alpha=q_m$ for
every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ and augment $Z_\bullet$ over the constant
simplicial space $X$.

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_p$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_m)\to H^j(A_p)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_p\to Z_m$. The maps $q_p:Z_p\to X$,
$q_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=g_1\cdots g_px$, satisfy $q_p\circ Z_\alpha=q_m$ for
every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ and augment $Z_\bullet$ over the constant
simplicial space $X$.

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_p$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_m)\to H^j(A_p)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

For an integer $n\ge1$, **complex projective space** is the set of complex lines in $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with the quotient topology
$$\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C):=(\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]:=\mathbb C^\times(z_0,\ldots,z_n).$$
The quotient projection is continuous and surjective. Its restriction to the unit sphere $S^{2n+1}\subset\mathbb C^{n+1}$ is still surjective, so $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ is compact. It is Hausdorff: the map sending a nonzero vector $z$ to the orthogonal projection $zz^*/\lVert z\rVert^2$ is continuous and constant on each complex line, hence descends by the quotient topology to a continuous injection from $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ into the Hausdorff space of complex matrices. A continuous injection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism onto its image.

For open $V\subseteq\mathbb C^r$, a map $H:V\to\mathbb C^s$ is **holomorphic** if at every $a\in V$ there is a complex-linear map $A_a:\mathbb C^r\to\mathbb C^s$ such that $H(a+h)=H(a)+A_a h+R_a(h)$ with $\lVert R_a(h)\rVert/\lVert h\rVert\to0$ as $h\to0$, $h\ne0$. When $r=1$, this is equivalent to each component being holomorphic in the sense of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]], since a finite vector of scalar difference quotients converges exactly when each component does. A complex atlas consists of charts into $\mathbb C^n$ with holomorphic transitions in both directions.

For $j\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ let $U_j:=\{[z_0:\cdots:z_n]:z_j\ne0\}$. These open sets cover projective space: their inverse images under the quotient projection are the open saturated sets where $z_j\ne0$. The **standard chart** is
$$\varphi_j:U_j\longrightarrow\mathbb C^n,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]\longmapsto (z_0/z_j,\ldots,\widehat{z_j/z_j},\ldots,z_n/z_j),$$
where the $j$th coordinate is omitted. It is well defined under rescaling. The coordinate-ratio map on the inverse image of $U_j$ is continuous and constant on each quotient fibre, so the quotient topology makes $\varphi_j$ continuous; its inverse inserts $1$ in the $j$th position and is continuous by composition with the quotient projection. Hence it is a homeomorphism. On $U_j\cap U_k$ the transition from the $j$th chart to the $k$th chart sends each coordinate $w_\ell=z_\ell/z_j$ ($\ell\ne j$) to $w_\ell/w_k$ for $\ell\ne k$, with the omitted $j$th coordinate equal to $1/w_k$. To check holomorphy at $a$ with $a_k\ne0$, set $a_j=1$ and $h_j=0$ for the omitted source coordinate. Each target coordinate has the expansion $(a_\ell+h_\ell)/(a_k+h_k)=a_\ell/a_k+h_\ell/a_k-a_\ell h_k/a_k^2+O(\lVert h\rVert^2)$ for $\ell\ne k$. The linear term is complex-linear, and the remainder estimate follows by expanding the reciprocal at the nonzero $a_k$. The inverse transition has the same form, so both are holomorphic. Thus these charts make $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ a complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ and a topological manifold of real dimension $2n$ in the sense of [[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]. The finite chart cover by second-countable copies of $\mathbb C^n$ gives a countable base. Its rational transition functions have smooth real coordinate expressions on their domains, so the atlas also defines the smooth structure in the sense of [[def-smooth-manifold]]. The space is path-connected: distinct lines represented by $u,v$ give the path $t\mapsto[(1-t)u+tv]$, whose vector never vanishes because $u,v$ are linearly independent; equal lines give a constant path. In particular, $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ is a Riemann surface in the sense of [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]].

A map $F:X\to\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ from a Riemann surface is **holomorphic** when it is continuous and every component of each chart expression $\varphi_j\circ F$, written in a local coordinate of $X$, is holomorphic on the open set $F^{-1}(U_j)$. On an overlap, the new components are $f_\ell/f_k$ and $1/f_k$, where the $f_\ell$ are the old components and $f_k\ne0$. The scalar quotient rule gives their holomorphy ([[thm-algebra-of-complex-derivatives]]), so it suffices to check one target chart locally. Changing the source coordinate composes each scalar component with a one-variable holomorphic chart transition, where [[thm-chain-rule-for-complex-derivatives]] applies ([[def-holomorphic-and-meromorphic-map-of-riemann-surfaces]]). A **projective line** is the image in $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ of a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$. Every invertible linear map of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ induces a holomorphic projective linear transformation: in source and target standard charts its coordinates are ratios of affine-linear functions with nonzero denominator, and the same reciprocal expansion gives a complex-linear derivative; these transformations act transitively on $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a scheme and let $n\ge0$. Then the
structure morphism
$$\pi:\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
is proper. No Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed on $S$, and the empty base is included.

Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

Fix the coordinate flag
$0\subset\mathbb F^1\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb F^N$. A **Schubert symbol**
for $\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ is a strictly increasing sequence
$a=(a_1<\cdots<a_n)$ with $1\leq a_i\leq N$. Its **Schubert cell** is

$$e(a)=\{W:\dim(W\cap\mathbb F^{a_i})=i,\ \dim(W\cap\mathbb F^{a_i-1})=i-1\text{ for every }i\}.$$

Every $W\in e(a)$ has a unique pivot-normalized basis

$$v_i=e_{a_i}+\sum_{\substack{j<a_i\\j\notin\{a_1,\ldots,a_{i-1}\}}}x_{ij}e_j,$$

after using earlier pivot rows to clear their columns. The free coordinates
number

$$d(a)=\sum_{i=1}^n(a_i-i),$$

so $e(a)\cong\mathbb F^{d(a)}$. Its real dimension is $d(a)$ for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and $2d(a)$ for $\mathbb F=\mathbb C$.
Equivalently, the integers $a_i-i$, read in reverse order, form a partition
fitting the $n$ by $(N-n)$ rectangle. These spaces use the Grassmannian
topology fixed in
[[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]].
For $n=0$, the unique symbol is the empty sequence, the displayed sum is the
empty sum $0$, and its Schubert cell is the one-point Grassmannian.

The Schubert strata are open cells whose closures are unions of cells with
componentwise smaller pivot symbols. They form a finite CW structure on
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$, and the standard inclusions
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\to
\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^{N+1})$ are cellular subcomplex inclusions.
Their union is the stated CW structure on
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)$, and each finite-dimensional
subcomplex is contained in a finite stage.
If $X$ has no cells in adjacent dimensions, every cellular differential is zero; consequently $H_n(X;G)\cong C_n^{\mathrm{cell}}(X;G)$.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here

$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$

Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and

approximation are supplied by

Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.

$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$. The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$u^*v^!\to v'^!u'^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$u'_!v'^*\cong v^*u_!$. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is

[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim

composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is

Here the right product is the external-product, refined middle-diagonal Thom intersection,

For an integer $n\ge1$, **complex projective space** is the set of complex lines in $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with the quotient topology
$$\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C):=(\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]:=\mathbb C^\times(z_0,\ldots,z_n).$$
The quotient projection is continuous and surjective. Its restriction to the unit sphere $S^{2n+1}\subset\mathbb C^{n+1}$ is still surjective, so $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ is compact. It is Hausdorff: the map sending a nonzero vector $z$ to the orthogonal projection $zz^*/\lVert z\rVert^2$ is continuous and constant on each complex line, hence descends by the quotient topology to a continuous injection from $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ into the Hausdorff space of complex matrices. A continuous injection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism onto its image.

For open $V\subseteq\mathbb C^r$, a map $H:V\to\mathbb C^s$ is **holomorphic** if at every $a\in V$ there is a complex-linear map $A_a:\mathbb C^r\to\mathbb C^s$ such that $H(a+h)=H(a)+A_a h+R_a(h)$ with $\lVert R_a(h)\rVert/\lVert h\rVert\to0$ as $h\to0$, $h\ne0$. When $r=1$, this is equivalent to each component being holomorphic in the sense of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]], since a finite vector of scalar difference quotients converges exactly when each component does. A complex atlas consists of charts into $\mathbb C^n$ with holomorphic transitions in both directions.

For $j\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ let $U_j:=\{[z_0:\cdots:z_n]:z_j\ne0\}$. These open sets cover projective space: their inverse images under the quotient projection are the open saturated sets where $z_j\ne0$. The **standard chart** is
$$\varphi_j:U_j\longrightarrow\mathbb C^n,\qquad [z_0:\cdots:z_n]\longmapsto (z_0/z_j,\ldots,\widehat{z_j/z_j},\ldots,z_n/z_j),$$
where the $j$th coordinate is omitted. It is well defined under rescaling. The coordinate-ratio map on the inverse image of $U_j$ is continuous and constant on each quotient fibre, so the quotient topology makes $\varphi_j$ continuous; its inverse inserts $1$ in the $j$th position and is continuous by composition with the quotient projection. Hence it is a homeomorphism. On $U_j\cap U_k$ the transition from the $j$th chart to the $k$th chart sends each coordinate $w_\ell=z_\ell/z_j$ ($\ell\ne j$) to $w_\ell/w_k$ for $\ell\ne k$, with the omitted $j$th coordinate equal to $1/w_k$. To check holomorphy at $a$ with $a_k\ne0$, set $a_j=1$ and $h_j=0$ for the omitted source coordinate. Each target coordinate has the expansion $(a_\ell+h_\ell)/(a_k+h_k)=a_\ell/a_k+h_\ell/a_k-a_\ell h_k/a_k^2+O(\lVert h\rVert^2)$ for $\ell\ne k$. The linear term is complex-linear, and the remainder estimate follows by expanding the reciprocal at the nonzero $a_k$. The inverse transition has the same form, so both are holomorphic. Thus these charts make $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ a complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ and a topological manifold of real dimension $2n$ in the sense of [[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]. The finite chart cover by second-countable copies of $\mathbb C^n$ gives a countable base. Its rational transition functions have smooth real coordinate expressions on their domains, so the atlas also defines the smooth structure in the sense of [[def-smooth-manifold]]. The space is path-connected: distinct lines represented by $u,v$ give the path $t\mapsto[(1-t)u+tv]$, whose vector never vanishes because $u,v$ are linearly independent; equal lines give a constant path. In particular, $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$ is a Riemann surface in the sense of [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]].

A map $F:X\to\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ from a Riemann surface is **holomorphic** when it is continuous and every component of each chart expression $\varphi_j\circ F$, written in a local coordinate of $X$, is holomorphic on the open set $F^{-1}(U_j)$. On an overlap, the new components are $f_\ell/f_k$ and $1/f_k$, where the $f_\ell$ are the old components and $f_k\ne0$. The scalar quotient rule gives their holomorphy ([[thm-algebra-of-complex-derivatives]]), so it suffices to check one target chart locally. Changing the source coordinate composes each scalar component with a one-variable holomorphic chart transition, where [[thm-chain-rule-for-complex-derivatives]] applies ([[def-holomorphic-and-meromorphic-map-of-riemann-surfaces]]). A **projective line** is the image in $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$ of a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$. Every invertible linear map of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ induces a holomorphic projective linear transformation: in source and target standard charts its coordinates are ratios of affine-linear functions with nonzero denominator, and the same reciprocal expansion gives a complex-linear derivative; these transformations act transitively on $\mathbb P^n(\mathbb C)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a scheme and let $n\ge0$. Then the
structure morphism
$$\pi:\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
is proper. No Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed on $S$, and the empty base is included.

Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

Fix the coordinate flag
$0\subset\mathbb F^1\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb F^N$. A **Schubert symbol**
for $\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ is a strictly increasing sequence
$a=(a_1<\cdots<a_n)$ with $1\leq a_i\leq N$. Its **Schubert cell** is

$$e(a)=\{W:\dim(W\cap\mathbb F^{a_i})=i,\ \dim(W\cap\mathbb F^{a_i-1})=i-1\text{ for every }i\}.$$

Every $W\in e(a)$ has a unique pivot-normalized basis

$$v_i=e_{a_i}+\sum_{\substack{j<a_i\\j\notin\{a_1,\ldots,a_{i-1}\}}}x_{ij}e_j,$$

after using earlier pivot rows to clear their columns. The free coordinates
number

$$d(a)=\sum_{i=1}^n(a_i-i),$$

so $e(a)\cong\mathbb F^{d(a)}$. Its real dimension is $d(a)$ for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and $2d(a)$ for $\mathbb F=\mathbb C$.
Equivalently, the integers $a_i-i$, read in reverse order, form a partition
fitting the $n$ by $(N-n)$ rectangle. These spaces use the Grassmannian
topology fixed in
[[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]].
For $n=0$, the unique symbol is the empty sequence, the displayed sum is the
empty sum $0$, and its Schubert cell is the one-point Grassmannian.

The Schubert strata are open cells whose closures are unions of cells with
componentwise smaller pivot symbols. They form a finite CW structure on
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$, and the standard inclusions
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\to
\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^{N+1})$ are cellular subcomplex inclusions.
Their union is the stated CW structure on
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)$, and each finite-dimensional
subcomplex is contained in a finite stage.
If $X$ has no cells in adjacent dimensions, every cellular differential is zero; consequently $H_n(X;G)\cong C_n^{\mathrm{cell}}(X;G)$.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be the analytic space of a smooth complex algebraic variety of pure dimension $d$, and let $q:A\to M$, $u:B\to M$ be morphisms of complex algebraic varieties with fiber product $T=A\times_MB$; write $a:T\to A$ and $b:T\to B$ for the projections, so that $qa=ub$ and the square is Cartesian. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor–Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]], [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $\mathrm{ex}:a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of the base-change morphism $u^*q_!\to b_!a^*$ of this square, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel–Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: The geometry and the cohomology of the projective line. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathrm{pt}\times_{\mathrm{pt}}\mathbb P^1=\mathbb P^1$. By [F3] the Schubert cells give $\mathbb P^1$ a finite CW structure with one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell and no cells in adjacent dimensions, so all cellular differentials vanish and the cellular cochain complex with coefficients $k$ is $k\oplus k[-2]$; by [F4] it computes $H^*(\mathbb P^1,k)$, so $H^0=k$, $H^1=0$, $H^2=k$, and since $k$ is a field the complex $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ is quasi-isomorphic to $k\oplus k[-2]$ (truncate and split the surjection of cocycles onto cohomology). Hence $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ and $L_1=k$.

The two classes. With $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$, the unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes the degree-$0$ summand $k$ with no shift, so $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)=\operatorname{Hom}(k,R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k))=H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)$ is the generator $1$ of that one-dimensional group. The evaluation $\beta:R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$ is the identity on the summand $k[1]$ and zero on the summand $k[-1]$; it generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_2,L_1)=\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1],k[1])=\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k),k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k,k)=k$, the other Hom-term $\operatorname{Hom}(k[-2],k)$ being zero. Then $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha:k\to k$ is evaluation of the constant class $1\in H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)$ at the point, hence is $\operatorname{id}_k$, and it is the only nonzero composite of these two generators.

The convolution check. Apply [F2] with $(i,j,k)=(1,2,1)$ and degrees $r=-1$, $s=1$ to the composable pair $\alpha:L_1\to L_2[r]$ and $\beta:L_2\to L_1[s]$: since $\beta[r]\circ\alpha=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ by step 2.1, the product theorem gives $\Phi_{11}^{0}(\operatorname{id}_k)=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$, so $\alpha*\beta=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention, and the right-hand side is the convolution product of [F1]. The corner degrees are $d_1+d_2-r=2$ for $\alpha$ and $d_2+d_1-s=0$ for $\beta$.

Under [F1], $\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)$ is the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_2(\mathbb P^1;k)$: the unit corresponds under the adjunction chain to the identity kernel of $k_{\mathbb P^1}$, whose class in $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_2(\mathbb P^1;k)=H^0(\mathbb P^1;k)=k$ is the positive generator, and $[\mathbb P^1]$ is that generator by the orientation normalization of [F5]. Likewise $\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$ is the normalized point class $[\mathrm{pt}]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_0(\mathbb P^1;k)=H^2(\mathbb P^1;k)$, the evaluation generator dual to the constant class. By [F2] the identity is sent to $[\Delta_{\mathrm{pt}}]=[\mathrm{pt}]\in H^{\mathrm{BM}}_0(Z_{11};k)$, so $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)=\Phi_{11}^0(\operatorname{id}_k)=[\mathrm{pt}]$.
